Article Title: CJP founder Abhijeet Dipke is a worker for AAP, how did he become a student: Kiren Rijiju
Article Text:
Rijiju said the government takes students’ concerns seriously, but stressed that student activism should not be confused with political opportunism.

(With agency inputs)





NEW DELHI: Union Parliamentary Affairs Minister Kiren Rijiju on Tuesday targeted Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke, alleging that he is an Aam Aadmi Party (AAP) worker trying to portray himself as a student leader amid the youth-led protests at Jantar Mantar.Rijiju told news agency ANI that the concerns raised by the protesting students were genuine, but alleged that the AAP had attempted to “hijack” the movement for its own political interests.Responding to a question on whether he welcomed the emergence of young leaders through the recent student-led movements, Rijiju said the government takes students’ concerns seriously, but stressed that student activism should not be confused with political opportunism."The students' concerns are valid, but the attempt by the Aam Aadmi Party and others to hijack the situation is not right. Abhijeet Dipke is from Maharashtra, but he is an Aam Aadmi Party worker. How did he become a 'student'?" he said.He added that the government remains open to engaging directly with students over their genuine demands, but accused political parties of exploiting the movement following electoral setbacks."Students have a certain passion, and one can engage in dialogue with them, but when political parties try to grind their own political axes by hiding behind students--that is simply not right," he said.Kiren Rijiju addressed perceptions about the BJP’s relationship with Gen Z, rejecting the notion that the party is out of touch with younger voters.He said traditional Asian cultural norms often encourage young people to listen to their elders, making generational alignment a gradual process. Rijiju stressed the need for continuous and active dialogue with Gen Z to bridge the generational gap."There is no lack of connection. They are our own children. Ours is an Asian society. People in Asia are bound together by family ties. It is not like Western society. We remain connected. We live in a family environment where children are expected to listen to their elders. If one keeps provoking them to simply keep making demands, it will take time to bridge that gap; we need to listen to them and also explain things to them. There must be a continuous dialogue," he said.Dipke had previously worked with the Aam Aadmi Party before launching the satirical Cockroach Janta Party (CJP), a movement that emerged following Chief Justice of India Surya Kant’s remarks about “cockroaches” and “parasites of society” during a Supreme Court hearing.Dipke’s old posts on X, dating from 2021 to 2024 and expressing support for the AAP, have further fuelled speculation about his current association with the party.The CJP has also conveyed that it is going to remain as a pressure group at present, stating, "We are not forming a political party; we will operate solely as a pressure group." It is currently conducting a 'School Thik Karo' campaign to highlight the issues present in government schools in villages.The massive CJP-led protest from June to July, which culminated in the resignation of then Union Education Minister Dharmendra Pradhan , also received support from several political parties, including the AAP and Samajwadi Party.
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju said the government takes students’ concerns seriously, but stressed that student activism should not be confused with political opportunism. He added that the government remains open to engaging directly with students over their genuine demands, but accused political parties of exploiting the movement following electoral setbacks.

Article Title: Is Ice Poseidon ‘wanted’ in Japan? Viral poster puts spotlight on streamer’s past police confrontations
Article Text:
Is Ice Poseidon ‘wanted’ in Japan? Viral poster puts spotlight on streamer’s past police confrontations

Paul Michael Joseph Denino faces no official wanted status in Japan

Ice Poseidon’s recent Japan trip and Pokémon store incident

Ice Poseidon is not officially wanted or under arrest in Japan, despite a “wanted poster” circulating online. The image was shared by DramaAlert on August 19, 2026, but there is no evidence that it is a Japanese police notice or that Paul Michael Joseph Denino has an active arrest warrant in the country. Japan’s National Police Agency publishes official wanted information, and Ice Poseidon does not appear on its listed wanted suspects. His recent livestreams also show him continuing to travel around Japan. The confusion comes from his past clashes with police, businesses and locals, along with unofficial citizen-made lists targeting nuisance streamers.The “wanted poster” should not be confused with an official Japanese police document. Japanese accounts that track foreign nuisance streamers have also discussed the image and questioned its wording. The account @canceljohnnys has separately posted about Ice Poseidon and his activities in Japan. These citizen-run accounts are not part of Japanese law enforcement.Ice Poseidon has faced several problems in Japan before. During his 2025 Japan and Korea livestream tour, police questioned him and another streamer after they picked and ate mandarins from trees without clear permission.Dexerto reported that about 14 officers became involved after a complaint, with translation devices used during the questioning. There was no reported arrest or criminal charge from that incident.He and other streamers were also stopped from boarding a ferry at Kagoshima during the same trip. JAPAN Forward reported that the group was refused boarding after previous incidents involving disruptive behaviour. (MThose incidents help explain why Ice Poseidon has appeared on citizen-created “wanted” or nuisance lists. One such list in February 2025 was titled “Harassing Japanese Locals” and included Ice Poseidon, Johnny Somali and other streamers. Dexerto reported that the list was created by a Japanese citizen, not the police.Ice Poseidon has returned to Japan in August 2026 and has continued streaming publicly. One recent incident involved a Pokémon store, where security stopped him after apparently recognising him from a photograph. He later returned wearing different clothes, a hat and sunglasses and managed to enter the store. The incident did not involve a reported police arrest or criminal charge.That distinction matters. A private store can refuse entry, while a citizen group can publish its own warning list. Neither action means someone is officially wanted by Japanese police.Ice Poseidon has faced more serious legal trouble in other countries. He was arrested in Thailand in 2023 over an explicit livestream incident, but that case was later dropped. That history is separate from his current situation in Japan.As of August 20, 2026, there is no verified evidence that Ice Poseidon has been arrested, formally charged or placed on an official Japanese wanted list. The poster circulating online should therefore not be presented as proof of an arrest warrant.
Article Summary: Paul Michael Joseph Denino faces no official wanted status in Japan. The confusion comes from his past clashes with police, businesses and locals. There is no verified evidence that Ice Poseidon has been arrested, formally charged or placed on an official Japanese wanted list.

Article Title: iPhone for her, bike for boyfriend: What led 13-year-old to plot grandfather’s murder
Article Text:
Police said two boys, wearing gloves, entered through a rear ventilator and opened the front door for their third accomplice.

Girl allegedly told boyfriend to kill grandfather

Teen boys allegedly entered house through ventilator

Contradictions in girl’s statements unravelled alleged plot

Cyber cell traces accused to Kollam within 24 hours





KOCHI: A 13-year-old girl and three teenage boys allegedly planned the murder of her 67-year-old grandfather in Kerala’s Alappuzha district to steal gold and money, with police saying the group intended to use the proceeds to buy an iPhone for the girl and a motorbike for her boyfriend.The girl’s boyfriend and two of his friends, all minors from Kollam, allegedly carried out the murder at her instigation, district police chief T K Vishnu Pratheep told reporters on Tuesday.He said the killing was carried out “in a professional manner, similar to what is seen in films.”Police said the group had two motives: to steal around 4.5 sovereigns of gold ornaments and to avenge restrictions the victim had imposed on the girl’s mobile phone use and friendships with boys.The girl had allegedly told her boyfriend that her grandfather had subjected her to “bad touch”, an allegation she had raised earlier, and that he needed to be killed.The victim lived with his wife, daughter and granddaughter at Haripad block panchayat in Alappuzha. On Thursday, his daughter, who was expecting a child, went to hospital accompanied by her mother.The murder took place on Saturday night after the girl allegedly told her grandfather that she needed to stay at a friend’s house to study for an exam and left.According to police, two of the boys, wearing gloves, entered the house through a rear ventilator opening and opened the front door to let the third accomplice in.They allegedly tied up the victim, beat him and smothered him on the dining room floor. Police said the girl watched the killing over a video call as it happened.A preliminary autopsy found smothering to be the cause of death.Before leaving, the accused allegedly took the gold ornaments and scattered chilli powder around the house to make investigators suspect a theft-only motive.The girl initially told police that she had visited the house twice on Sunday, knocked on the door and left after receiving no response. She said she then called her grandfather’s phone, which was engaged, informed her mother and returned to her friend’s house.She returned on Monday morning and, after again receiving no response, alerted neighbours. The victim was subsequently found dead inside the house, with his hands and legs tied with cloth.Police initially suspected close relatives and outsiders. However, contradictions in the girl’s statements, including a claimed alibi that did not hold up during questioning, led investigators to suspect her boyfriend and his friends.Phone records and other evidence helped police unravel her version within hours.Cyber cell investigators traced the accused to Kollam within 24 hours using mobile tower location data. Police said one ring from the stolen ornaments was sold for Rs 16,000 at a jewellery shop in Kollam, and the person who allegedly helped broker the sale has been identified.The remaining stolen gold was recovered by Tuesday morning, police said. The accused will be produced before the Juvenile Justice Board.Police attributed the alleged crime to a mix of cinematic influence and family problems. During questioning, the girl also told police that a lack of affection from her parents had weighed on her.
Article Summary: Girl allegedly told boyfriend to kill grandfather. Teen boys allegedly entered house through ventilator. Contradictions in girl’s statements unravelled alleged plot.Cyber cell traces accused to Kollam within 24 hours using mobile tower location data.

Article Title: Trouble brewing for Zelenskyy? Ex-defence minister calls for wartime polls
Article Text:
Ukraine has been under martial law since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022

Why Fedorov’s election call matters

Why a wartime election would be extremely difficult

Zelenskyy faces a wider political test

Ukraine’s recently dismissed former defence minister Mykhailo Fedorov has called for presidential elections to be held despite the ongoing war with Russia, delivering one of the most direct political challenges to President Volodymyr Zelenskyy since the full-scale invasion began in 2022.In a nine-minute video address posted online, Fedorov argued that Ukraine must restore a “full democratic process” even while fighting Russia. “Democracy cannot be held hostage by Russia. We are fighting precisely because we want to remain a free European state,” the 35-year-old said. Although he did not name Zelenskyy, his remarks amounted to a sharp criticism of the way the country is being governed, including concerns over corruption, appointments and a lack of accountability.Fedorov’s intervention comes weeks after Zelenskyy abruptly removed him as defence minister, only six months after his appointment. His dismissal triggered rare wartime protests in Kyiv and has fuelled speculation about growing tensions within Ukraine’s political establishment. Zelenskyy has not publicly responded to the call for elections.Ukraine has been under martial law since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, and elections are suspended under the country’s legal framework.Zelenskyy’s five-year presidential term formally expired in May 2024, but the continuation of martial law has prevented a vote from taking place.Fedorov argued that the prolonged war should not permanently put democratic politics on hold. “We must find a legal, safe and realistic mechanism that will allow Ukraine to restore a full democratic process even amid a prolonged war,” he said.The appeal could prove politically significant because Fedorov is not an outsider. A former digital minister and one of the prominent young reformers in Zelenskyy’s team, he played a key role in Ukraine’s wartime adoption of drone technology and other innovations. His sudden removal, reportedly amid tensions with military leadership, had already exposed divisions within the government.Recent polling cited in the material suggests Fedorov could emerge as a serious contender in a future presidential race. He was placed behind Zelenskyy and former armed forces chief Valerii Zaluzhnyi in a first-round scenario, but polling indicated that both Fedorov and Zaluzhnyi could defeat Zelenskyy in a run-off.Holding an election while the war continues would present enormous logistical and security challenges. Russian missile and drone attacks regularly target Ukrainian cities, while fighting stretches across a front line of more than 1,200km.Millions of Ukrainians have also been displaced. More than 4 million are living under temporary protection in the European Union, while millions more are internally displaced. Around 1 million people are serving in Ukraine’s defence forces, including personnel deployed near the frontline.The situation is further complicated by Russian occupation of roughly a fifth of Ukraine. Ensuring voting rights for people in occupied areas, protecting polling stations and preventing Russian interference would all require new legal and security arrangements.A Ukrainian political analyst cited in the material said there was a deep-rooted view that elections were necessary, but only after the “hot phase” of the war ended. Even Fedorov’s supporters face the question of how a genuinely free and safe vote could be organised while Russian attacks continue.Fedorov’s intervention comes as Zelenskyy faces renewed scrutiny over corruption and the functioning of his administration. Ukraine’s anti-corruption agencies have launched a probe involving current and former officials, including an unnamed official in the presidential office. Zelenskyy subsequently dismissed deputy presidential office head Iryna Mudra, although investigators have not named her as a suspect.The developments add to political pressure on a president whose popularity, while still significant, has fallen from its extraordinary wartime levels. The latest controversy also follows previous public anger over government attempts to curb the powers of anti-corruption agencies.
Article Summary: Ukraine has been under martial law since Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022. President Volodymyr Zelenskyy’s five-year presidential term formally expired in May 2024, but the continuation of martial law has prevented a vote from taking place.

Article Title: Volhynia massacres: Russia using WWII to plant discord between Ukraine and Poland?
Article Text:
Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres.

How Russia is 'exploiting' the Volhynia dispute

The facts may be real, but the narrative can still be manipulated

Ukraine fatigue creates fertile ground for the campaign

Russia is being accused of using a painful chapter in the history of Poland and Ukraine to deepen tensions between the two countries, as Warsaw and Kyiv remain divided over the killings that took place during World War 2.Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging in Poland around the Volhynia massacres, while also using the issue to fuel anger against Ukrainians living in the country.The campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say the aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.The historical dispute centres on the Volhynia massacres between 1943 and 1945. Poland says Ukrainian nationalists killed around 100,000 Poles during the violence, while thousands of Ukrainians were also killed in retaliatory attacks.Tensions over the issue increased after Ukrainian President Volodymyr Zelenskyy named an army unit after insurgents linked to the massacres. Polish president Karol Nawrocki, who is from the political right, responded by stripping Zelenskyy of a major Polish honour in June.Polish deputy digital minister Pawel Olszewski said the disagreement was quickly followed by a surge in Russian messaging across social media and Russian media platforms, including Telegram.Research by the state-backed Polish Institute of International Affairs found that Polish-language anti-Ukrainian content on X, Facebook, Instagram, TikTok and YouTube rose by more than 250% after Zelenskyy's decision.Filip Bryjka of PISM said much of this increase appeared to have been artificially boosted through bots, creating the impression that anti-Ukrainian sentiment was spreading rapidly.Analysts say one reason this type of campaign is difficult to detect is that it does not necessarily depend on completely fabricated information.Instead, genuine events and historical grievances can be repeatedly highlighted and framed in ways that encourage anger towards a particular group."The event is real, but the interpretation is imposed by an external actor," said Wojciech Pokora, an analyst at Info Ops Poland Foundation.Moscow has rejected the accusations. The Russian embassy in Warsaw said Russia does not interfere in relations between other countries."The Russian Federation does not interfere in the relations between other states," the Russian embassy in Warsaw said in an emailed statement, adding that accusations about Russia spreading disinformation to undermine support for Ukraine are baseless.The issue has gained greater importance because Poland remains one of Ukraine's strongest supporters in its war against Russia, but public backing for Ukraine has weakened.An IBRiS poll published last month found that 33.6% of respondents said their attitude towards Ukrainians had worsened following the latest dispute linked to the World War Two killings.Another IBRiS survey found that support for continuing military assistance to Ukraine had fallen to 52%, compared with 78% in 2022.Researchers caution that declining support for Ukraine cannot be blamed entirely on Russian influence.Poland is home to an estimated 1.8 to 1.9 million Ukrainian migrants, while disagreements over grain imports and the unresolved legacy of the Volhynia killings have also contributed to public frustration.Olszewski said the Russian messaging had "fallen on fertile ground".Meanwhile, hostility towards Ukrainians in Poland has reportedly increased, prompting prime minister Donald Tusk to call for an end to xenophobic attacks.The issue could become even more politically significant ahead of Poland's 2027 parliamentary elections. Polling suggests Tusk's pro-European government could struggle to retain power, while support for the far-right has been growing.That makes the Volhynia dispute more than a historical argument. For Poland, it touches on a painful national memory. For Ukraine, it is part of a complicated shared history with its neighbour. And for Russia, Polish analysts argue, the disagreement offers an opportunity to deepen divisions between two countries that have otherwise stood together against Moscow.
Article Summary: Polish officials and researchers say Moscow has sharply increased online messaging around the Volhynia massacres. Campaign has largely played out on social media, with much of the content appearing in Polish. Analysts say aim is not always to create completely false stories, but to amplify real disputes in ways that can deepen existing divisions.

Article Title: Zeeshan Siddique gets death threat from Portugal number, caller claims Godara gang link
Article Text:
NCP leader Zeeshan Siddique reported receiving a death threat from a Portugal-based number (File photo)





MUMBAI: National Congress Party leader and MLC Zeeshan Siddique filed a complaint soon after he arrived in Mumbai on Friday morning after a fresh threat he received while he was in London at 2.36 (which was 7.06 am IST).Bandra police registered a non-cognisable (NC) offence against an unknown person based on an audio threat he received on August 12.Siddique received the threat audio clip from a Portugal number.Siddique confirmed TOI that Bandra police registered an NC based on the complaint he submitted."The audio threat that lasted 1.29 minutes was received on my WhatsApp number by the same person who identified himself as Zeeshan Akhtar. My sister filed the first NC on August 6 while I was abroad. Now, the death threat audio clip was sent directly to me using Portugal number. In November 2025, we filed the writ and soon my security cover was reduced from eight cops to two. Also, there was 22 cops deployed at my residence which was reduced to zero," he said.The person who sent the audio threat dared Siddique to go and file a police complaint himself instead of sending his sister forward to file the complaint and threatened he will the one to kill him.TOI extracts the transcript of the threat audio which states, "Listen here, Zeeshan Siddique, this is Zeeshan Akhtar speaking. Listen to me carefully: I am going to kill you. Before I even touch your father... well, I had already assigned a team to the task two years ago, back when I was in police custody, got it?""Brother, everyone I’ve killed, I did so openly. Now, your end has come. Don't push your sister to the forefront; if you have the guts, go file the complaint yourself. I know everything; I’m aware of every detail. You might not die today or tomorrow, but within a year, you will definitely die. I have no problem with your money and I am not threatening you for money. The person claimed that he object to my illegal business and for which he will kill me. He threatened: 'You will die, and I am the one who will kill you'," the transcript stated further.The first threat compaint was filed by Siddique's sister Arshia on August 6. She was in the Bombay High Court (HC) for the hearing of a writ petition filed for initiating action against a builder whose role is suspected behind their father's murder."This is not coincidence. Both the threats are being made when the dates for the writ petition was nearing," he said.DCP (West Zone-2) Mohit Garg confirmed about the fresh NC registered on complaint from Siddique.A case of criminal intimidation involving severe threats, such as threatening death and grievous hurt was registered against unknown person.
Article Summary: Siddique received the threat audio clip from a Portugal-based number. Bandra police registered a non-cognisable (NC) offence against an unknown person. The person who sent the audio threat dared Siddique to go and file a police complaint himself instead of sending his sister forward to file the complaint.

Article Title: ‘We can drive them crazy’: Rahul Gandhi takes aim at PM Modi, Amit Shah
Article Text:
Rahul addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

In a statement suggesting that students’ protest and the Parliament session washout have the ruling BJP at a loss for strategy, Congress leader Rahul Gandhi said “we” will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Kharge said Gujarat produced visionary leaders, but now “these two” are ruining everything.Rahul said the country is witnessing a fight between “those who give orders and those who want to express themselves”, adding that the country has started expressing itself after a lot of people behaved like “cowards” against the combine of RSS-BJP for a long time.“Our job is to make India express itself and break that order,” the Congress leader said, adding “we will drive them crazy”.Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress, that seeks to create a common political strategy with non-Congress platforms of people’s struggle.Rahul said Modi is unable to sleep at night while Amit Shah, who was eulogised as Chanakya, did not come to Parliament for 20 days. “Because for the first time, they are feeling India’s expression. They realise this country will not stop expressing itself.It will break the RSS order.”“Till Modi and Shah give their resignations, they will not be able to sleep, we will keep them awake,” he said.He lashed out at the RSS as a “bunch of jokers”, and said the organisation has been reduced to being an instrument of big capital like Adani and Ambani, far from its original base of small businesses.The leader of opposition said Modi has messed up India’s national security and foreign policy, the latter because of the ignorant idea that he is making friends with the world leaders and foreign policy is about hugging them. He said Modi thought foreign leaders were his friends, and “they caught him”. He said India squandered a great opportunity presented by the Iran war to play the mediator, and the role was usurped by Pakistan.In what had the large audience from across the country in splits, Rahul illustrated Modi’s hugging by giving a bear hug to Rachnatmak Congress chief Sandeep Dikshit - who in turn asked Rahul jokingly “if he had thought he was hugging Italian PM Meloni”, and by enacting other practical jokes. He also cited a childhood anecdote of how then PM Indira Gandhi did not take seriously the US administration’s attempt to flatter her via the then First Lady.
Article Summary: Rahul Gandhi said ‘we’ will not relent till PM Narendra Modi and home minister Amit Shah quit power under pressure. Party chief Mallikarjun Kharge said Modi and Shah will destroy the country and not leave anything for the coming generations. Rahul and Kharge addressed a conclave of Rachnatmak Congress.

Article Title: F-16 fighter jet crashes in Turkey during training flight, pilot safe
Article Text: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova on Wednesday, Chinese state news agency Xinhua reported.According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft.In a statement posted on social media, the ministry said the aircraft went down during a routine training mission and that the pilot safely bailed out before the crash.The exact cause of the accident will be determined following a detailed investigation, the ministry added.A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site following the incident, local media reported.Live footage broadcast by Turkish news channel NTV showed a fireball and thick black smoke rising from the wreckage, visible from several locations across the province.
Article Summary: A Turkish Air Force F-16 fighter jet crashed during a training flight in the northwestern province of Yalova. According to the defence ministry, the pilot survived the crash after safely ejecting from the aircraft. A large number of ambulances and medical rescue teams were dispatched to the crash site.

Article Title: Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp, Walt Nauta: 3 aides were allowed with Trump when he was moved into a catering truck during Turkey emergency
Article Text:
Dan Scavino, Natalie Harp and Walt Nauta are the closest aides allowed inside the catering truck that hid President Donald Trump in Turkey.

Who is Dan Scavino?

Who is Natalie Harp?

Who is Walt Nauta?

No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Apart from some low-ranking aides, only three individuals were allowed inside the truck, as they are believed to be the closest to the president: Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations. Washington Post reported that neither Marco Rubio nor Pete Hegseth nor Stephen Miller were allowed inside the truck that took TrumpThe catering truck moved under concealment from the Air Force One aircraft to a smaller Air Force C-32A before flying to Britain separately.Dan Scavino has been serving as the White House deputy chief of staff in the second Trump administration but his history with Trump dates back to 1992, when he worked as a caddie at a New York country club that Trump later purchased and turned into Trump National Golf Club Westchester. After graduating from college, Scavino worked his way up to become the golf club's general manager.He joined Trump's 2016 presidential campaign and went on to serve throughout the entire first Trump administration as White House Director of Social Media and later Deputy Chief of Staff for Communications.During that time, he was particularly known for managing Trump's personal social media presence and online strategy. He remained a central advisor at Mar-a-Lago following the 2020 election, worked as a senior official on the 2024 campaign, and returned to senior White House leadership upon Trump taking office again in 2025.Natalie Harp is an American political aide and former television presenter who serves as Executive Assistant to the President in Donald Trump's second White House administration. She is the one who handles the president's daily schedule and is always spotted with him. Known colloquially among campaign staffers and media outlets as Trump's "human printer," Harp earned a reputation for constantly accompanying him with a portable printer to feed him printed news articles, polls, and favorable commentary. In her role as executive assistant, she remains a member of his inner circle, assisting with his daily schedule and managing dictation for his social media accounts.Walt Nauta is a close political aide to Donald Trump and currently serves in his second White House administration as Deputy Assistant to the President and Director of Oval Office Operations. Nauta spent 20 years in the U.S. Navy, reaching the rank of Senior Chief Petty Officer. During his military career, he was assigned to the Presidential Food Service and eventually became a White House valet during Trump's first presidency. In that role, he acted as a personal assistant and "body man," handling day-to-day tasks like fetching beverages and managing travel details.After Trump left office in 2021, Nauta retired from the Navy and joined Trump's personal staff at Mar-a-Lago, continuing to work as his primary executive assistant and political aide. He later drew widespread national attention when he was indicted alongside Trump in June 2023 in the federal classified documents case, where prosecutors accused him of helping move and conceal boxes of sensitive materials.
Article Summary: No cabinet officials were allowed inside the catering truck, inside which President Donald Trump was snuck away last month in response to a potential Iranian assassination threat in Turkey. Dan Scavino, the White House deputy chief of staff; Natalie Harp, Trump's assistant and Walt Nauta, the director of Oval Office operations, are believed to be the closest aides to the president.

Article Title: Thailand visit, Suu Kyi access: Can Myanmar’s Min Aung Hlaing win political legitimacy?
Article Text:
Min Aung Hlaing in Thailand; Aung San Suu Kyi with ICRC official

Min Aung Hlaing's ascent to power

Significance of Aung San Suu Kyi

Why Thailand visit matters for Min Aung Hlaing - and how Bangkok differs from ASEAN

Can regional engagement help Min Aung Hlaing’s legitimacy push?

Min Aung Hlaing’s continuing legitimacy challenge

Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week, in a trip that carried significance beyond routine diplomacy. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency.That visit to Thailand coincided with another significant development in Myanmar. Aung San Suu Kyi , the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor. On August 3, Suu Kyi met Arnaud de Baecque, the International Committee of the Red Cross' (ICRC) resident representative in her country.Naypyidaw also released photographs of the meeting—the first official images of the former State Counsellor in years.Was the close timing of the two developments just a coincidence? For Min Aung Hlaing, who came to power by overthrowing an elected government rather than through the ballot box, both developments could be part of a broader effort to build political legitimacy and gain wider international acceptance.During his visit to Thailand, the 70-year-old former military leader sought to reassure his host, Thai Prime Minister Anutin Charnvirakul, that Myanmar was “returning to democracy.”"Myanmar has now re-established itself on the path to democracy and is moving toward a better future," Min Aung Hlaing told Charnvirakul.The remarks stood in sharp contrast to the circumstances of his rise to the presidency. His claim that Myanmar is on a “democratic path” also comes against the backdrop of a bloody civil war triggered by the coup that brought him to power.According to the Assistance Association for Political Prisoners, an independent organisation that documents arrests and casualties linked to the Myanmar civil war, more than 8,200 civilians had been killed and 31,645 people arrested by the regime's security forces as of August 5.Besides, the parliamentary elections under Min Aung Hlaing in late 2025 and early 2026 were also widely criticised as “neither free nor fair” as the army-backed Union Solidarity and Development Party swept the elections, winning 232 of the 263 contested seats in the lower house and 109 of 157 seats in the upper house. Ahead of the presidential election in April—Myanmar's first since 2018—he resigned from the military and was subsequently elected president.However, his transition to the presidency did little to ease international scepticism. Major democracies withheld congratulations following his victory.For Myanmar, Aung San Suu Kyi’s significance extends beyond her role as the head of the country’s first democratically elected civilian government in 50 years and the military’s toppling of her administration.For many inside and outside Myanmar, the 1991 Nobel Peace Prize laureate remains the country's most recognisable symbol of democratic rule and civilian legitimacy.In 2022, Suu Kyi was sentenced to 33 years in prison on a series of charges that her supporters and rights groups described as “politically motivated” and intended to prevent her return to politics. Later, her sentence was reduced to 27 years and, in April, to 18 years, while she was transferred to house arrest.Against this backdrop, the meeting with the ICRC representative was significant because it marked the first confirmed contact between Suu Kyi, 81, and an independent international organisation since her house arrest. It was also her first confirmed communication with the outside world since she wrote a letter to her son from prison in early 2024.Sreeparna Banerjee, an Associate Fellow at the Observer Research Foundation (ORF), agreed that both developments could be seen as part of Myanmar’s broader effort to “manage its international image,” but said it cannot be assumed that the moves were directly linked.“The timing is noteworthy, but it would be difficult to establish a direct connection between the two developments at this stage… Access to Aung San Suu Kyi after a prolonged period of isolation could signal some limited openness, while Min Aung Hlaing’s high-profile visit to Thailand demonstrates Myanmar’s attempt to expand diplomatic engagement,” Banerjee, whose work focuses on Myanmar and Thailand, told The Times of India.For Min Aung Hlaing, the bigger challenge remains turning such diplomatic engagement into wider political legitimacy and international acceptance.According to Banerjee, the visit was important for Min Aung Hlaing because it offered him a degree of political normalisation.“Being received at the highest level by an ASEAN neighbour allows him to project the image of a leader whose government is once again engaging with the region rather than remaining diplomatically isolated,” she said.Significantly, while Thailand and Myanmar are both ASEAN member states, Bangkok’s approach towards Naypyidaw differs from that of the rest of the 11-nation bloc of Southeast Asian states.Thailand has continued to engage with Myanmar despite ASEAN barring Min Aung Hlaing from its top-level meetings over the non-implementation of the Five-Point Consensus agreed with the grouping after he seized power.On this, Banerjee observed that the real value of Bangkok’s “bridge” diplomacy — acting as a bridge between Myanmar and ASEAN — would depend on whether Thailand can use it to encourage some meaningful progress on the Five-Point Consensus.Additionally, ASEAN is yet to recognise the results of Myanmar’s 2025–26 parliamentary elections. The bloc has also repeatedly called for Suu Kyi’s unconditional release, renewing the demand after her meeting with the ICRC official. The regime rebuffed this call too.For its part, Thailand has described its approach vis-à-vis Myanmar as one of “calibrated re-engagement” aimed at keeping dialogue open while responding to “realities on the ground.” Bangkok has also argued that Myanmar is essential to ASEAN unity and regional stability, provided it remains peaceful and stable.In addition to being barred from top-level ASEAN summits, Min Aung Hlaing faces Western sanctions over his role in toppling Suu Kyi’s government, the subsequent civil war, and the alleged persecution of the Rohingya minority in the Rakhine province.The Thailand visit was his fourth overseas trip since becoming president, following visits to India, China, and Laos. India was the only democratic country among the four destinations, underscoring the limited engagement he has so far had with democratic governments.Despite this, and close ties with Russia, he has remained largely isolated internationally.So, can his engagement with Thailand and his wider regional outreach — help him in his bid for greater international recognition and acceptance?Sreeparna Banerjee, the ORF Associate Fellow, suggested that even regional acceptance remains uncertain at this stage, despite such engagement being an important part of Myanmar’s quest for political legitimacy.“Naypyidaw appears determined to engage on its own terms rather than fully follow the ASEAN framework. Thailand's outreach may create space for dialogue, but whether this translates into wider regional acceptance remains uncertain,” she explained.She also highlighted that uncertainty over Myanmar’s regional acceptance stems in part from the fact that Singapore will take over the ASEAN chairmanship in 2027. The city-state has repeatedly called for full implementation of the Five-Point Consensus.This underscores the scale of the challenge facing Min Aung Hlaing in his bid for wider acceptance.For a leader who rises to power as Min Aung Hlaing did, securing international recognition is likely to remain a gradual and difficult process.The regime’s refusal to release Suu Kyi, a global icon, further complicates that effort.Engagement with neighbouring countries can provide an important opening, but broader recognition often depends on how other governments assess the resulting political situation. Yet for Min Aung Hlaing, this remains the only option to secure recognition.For now, engagement with Thailand may offer Min Aung Hlaing some diplomatic space, but whether it can translate into legitimacy for him remains uncertain.
Article Summary: Myanmar President Min Aung Hlaing made a two-day state visit to Thailand last week. He remains internationally isolated because, in his earlier role as supreme commander of Myanmar’s armed forces, he led the 2021 coup that overthrew the elected civilian government. He subsequently ruled as head of the junta for five years before formally assuming the presidency. Aung San Suu Kyi, the former leader whose government was ousted in that coup, was allowed to receive a visitor.

Article Title: ‘Manan, it’s done bro’: CJP’s Abhijeet Dipke calls ‘Legal Cockroaches’ to protest, seek BCI chief’s resignation
Article Text:
Cockroach Janta Party (CJP) founder Abhijeet Dipke and BCI chief Manan Kumar Mishra





NEW DELHI: A protest has been called against Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman Manan Kumar Mishra over the council’s now-withdrawn directive concerning students of NALSAR University of Law, with the All India Young Advocates Association (AIYAA) set to stage a demonstration on Thursday.Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ), also invited lawyers to join the protest. Sharing a post on X, Dipke wrote: “Manan, it’s done bro! All legal cockroaches must join this protest.”CJP national spokesperson Saurav Das said on X that “Legal Cockroaches” would come together to protest against Mishra and demand his resignation. The demonstration is scheduled for 10am.“The protest has been called by the All India Young Advocates Association. I support any form of peaceful protest that seeks accountability and sets high standards for conduct in office,” Das wrote.Ratna Singh, legal affairs head of the CJP, also backed the protest, saying “Legal Cockroaches are coming together tomorrow to demand accountability from the BCI Chairman.”“In a democracy, every form of peaceful protest is legitimate and welcome. The legal fraternity must recognise that every voice matters and that demanding answers and accountability is not only our right, but our responsibility,” Singh wrote on X.The protest comes days after Mishra apologised to law students over a controversial BCI order concerning graduating students of NALSAR.In a statement issued on Independence Day, Mishra expressed regret if any of his words or communication had hurt students’ feelings.“If anything connected with the present controversy, any of my words, or letter, has hurt the feelings of our law students, I sincerely regret and apologise for the same,” Mishra had said.The controversy began after some NALSAR students wrote to the university’s vice chancellor, registrar and professors opposing a proposal to invite Chief Justice of India Surya Kant as chief guest at the university’s convocation.The BCI had initially directed state bar councils not to enrol students from the current graduating batch of NALSAR as advocates. Mishra had said the council was examining allegations surrounding a campaign against the CJI’s participation in the convocation and had sought a report identifying those allegedly responsible.The directive was withdrawn within hours following criticism from members of the legal fraternity. A subsequent modified order clarified that the “vast majority” of students were innocent and should not be made to suffer for the alleged misconduct of a few.CJI Surya Kant later criticised the BCI’s action, describing the matter as a “dialogue between students and me”. The NALSAR Student Bar Council subsequently sought a public apology from Mishra.Graduating students, current students and alumni of NLSIU, Bengaluru, also issued a joint statement seeking an apology and opposing the presence of the BCI chairman and the CJI at their convocation.In his Independence Day statement, Mishra said students of National Law Universities were among the country’s most informed and discerning young citizens and that their views could carry significance beyond individual controversies.He maintained that peaceful protest and disagreement were part of a constitutional democracy, while urging students to reconsider their position if further facts or clarifications emerged.Mishra also said attending or abstaining from a convocation was ultimately a student’s choice and appealed against giving the controversy a “political or extraneous colour through outside influence”.The AIYAA’s proposed protest brings the demand for Mishra’s resignation into sharper focus, with Das also claiming that the Bombay Bar Association had called for his resignation.(With agency inputs)
Article Summary: A protest has been called against Bar Council of India (BCI) chairman Manan Kumar Mishra over the council’s now-withdrawn directive concerning students of NALSAR University of Law. The All India Young Advocates Association (AIYAA) set to stage a demonstration on Thursday. Abhijeet Dipke, founder of the Cockroach Janta Party ( CJP ), also invited lawyers to join the protest.

Article Title: ‘Pipeline leak complaint made days ago’: CNG station blast during truck refuelling kills 3 in Delhi
Article Text:
The blast damaged the refuelling equipment as well

CNG station blast in Tikri

‘Complaint about a leak in pipeline made 20 days ago’





NEW DELHI: Three people were killed and three critically injured after a truck’s CNG cylinder exploded while it was being refilled at a gas station in Outer Delhi’s Tikri on Wednesday.All the dead were workers at the gas station located near Tikri Metro Station.Police said the exact cause of the explosion was not immediately known and are examining the truck cylinder and gas station equipment.The blast, which happened around 3.20 pm, completely damaged the cylinder as well as the refuelling equipment at the station. Fire officials said a car and a scooter in the vicinity were also damaged in the blast.The dead were identified as Manish (25), Brahmjeet (34) and Sunny (30).Manish’s relative Vijay Prasad said Manish had been working at the gas station for three years and was from Bihar. He is survived by his wife, a five-month-old child and parents.Manish’s friend Ashish Srivastava said it was a struggle to get the blast victims to hospital. Manish lay bleeding at the filling station for around 30 minutes as no ambulance was available, he said.He claimed the CNG station had given the employees two days off around 20 days ago to fix a complaint about a leak in the refuelling pipeline.There was no immediate response from the filling station operator on the allegation.Anil Chhikara, former deputy transport commissioner of Delhi, said CNG cylinders are not being tested every 3 years, and fake certification is being issued. In Delhi and NCR, CNG stations issue certificates without physically inspecting the vehicles. Further, Delhi govt does not oversee CNG testing stations, he said.Aditya, a relative of the deceased Brahmjeet, said that two of his uncles worked at the CNG filling station. One of them was killed in the blast, while the other sustained injuries. “Both were married and had children. They had been working at the station for the past two years,” he said.Sunny’s cousin Balraj Singh said Sunny had been working at the station for the past three to four years. Sunny’s elder brother had died in an accident, and he was supporting his brother’s children and family. He was the sole breadwinner of the family, Singh said.
Article Summary: Three people were killed and three critically injured after a truck’s CNG cylinder exploded while it was being refilled at a gas station in Outer Delhi. The dead were identified as Manish (25), Brahmjeet (34) and Sunny (30) Police said the exact cause of the explosion was not immediately known.

Article Title: CBI insignia, fake IDs, WhatsApp notice: How Delhi bizman’s wife foiled ‘Special 26’-style raid
Article Text:
Fake CBI raid attempt foiled (Image Credit: X)





NEW DELHI: A suspected ‘Special 26’-style fake CBI raid was foiled at a businessman’s residence in Delhi’s Rohini after his wife refused to open the gate for a group of people claiming to be CBI officers.According to a complaint filed with the police, around eight to 10 people arrived at the residence and said they had come to conduct a CBI search. They allegedly tried to enter the house without showing proper authorisation or establishing their identities.The woman refused to let them in despite alleged pressure and threats to open the gate. The group then remained outside the house for around 1.5 hours, according to the complaint.Neighbours gathered at the spot and questioned the group about the search warrant and other authorisation. When asked to provide a copy of the notice, the alleged fake officers reportedly said the document was in their car and left the spot on the pretext of bringing it.The family subsequently called the police helpline 112, following which a police team reached the residence.The complaint states that the suspected fake officers were wearing clothes bearing the CBI insignia and carrying identity cards claiming they were CBI officials.A notice purportedly bearing the name and signature of the CBI Director was later sent to the complainant’s father on WhatsApp.Although the message was subsequently deleted, the family had taken a screenshot and submitted it to police along with the complaint.The family has alleged that the notice was fabricated and was intended to make the group’s purported action appear to be an official CBI operation.The incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed near the residence. Police are examining the footage and investigating the matter.
Article Summary: A suspected ‘Special 26’-style fake CBI raid was foiled at a businessman’s residence. His wife refused to open the gate for a group of people claiming to be CBI officers. The incident was captured on CCTV cameras installed near the residence.
